rationale: Record the first PNG golden in the visual harness. All five committed goldens were Yoga layout JSON, so the harness made raster claims through a gate that compared nothing; the PNG plumbing in spec.py and runner.py had never been exercised by a fixture. This adds canvas2d/raster-determinism, a text-free fixture whose drawing is declared as an ops array so the golden's content is reviewable in the fixture diff, with its sha256 recorded in tools/harness/visual/pins.py beside the existing font and release-asset digests. Rasterization goes through the pinned skia-python wheel rather than pulp::view::render_to_png, because render_to_png resolves to CoreGraphics on Apple and Skia elsewhere (per-platform bytes by construction) and both visual-harness.yml smoke jobs are pytest lanes with no Pulp C++ build. Fixtures opt in with driver: declarative_raster, leaving the existing kind: render capture semantics untouched. Cross-host byte identity is stated as unproven: darwin-arm64 and darwin-x86_64 under Rosetta were measured identical, linux-x86_64 is deliberately absent from RASTER_GOLDEN_VERIFIED_PLATFORMS, and both jobs publish the digest they computed so the first Linux run either confirms or disproves it. This changes only the proof harness and its own workflow; no render surface, backend, importer, asset pipeline, or shipped output moves, and no accepted expansion boundary or Vellum source authority is touched, so the disposition is watch-only. design-output-and-packaging is crossed by exactly one file, docs/status/tools.yaml, which is a named selector for that family. tools/harness/visual/raster.py carries a __main__ guard and an argparse CLI, so the tools registry sweep classifies it as an agent-invocable entry point and rejects it as unregistered; the entry registers the digest reporter and CLAUDE.md carries the generated digest of that registry. No importer, DesignIR schema, codegen output, CLI command, packaging artifact or release workflow changes, so the family is crossed by a registry row and nothing it is about moves.
